correctness.claim_boundary: Observed output identity for the six Camelid POPC-on/off requests; no claim that every internal kernel or intermediate logit is bit-exact to a legacy serial or BMMA implementation. The vendor run used the same request shape and prompt-token count but produced different coherent wording, so no cross-engine output-parity claim is made.

measurement_notes: Decode tokens per second is 23 post-first tokens divided by the measured post-first interval; the first generated token is excluded.
Image TTFT includes image projection, prompt prefill, and production of the first generated token, so it is reported separately from decode throughput.
Measurements are same-host three-run engineering benchmarks for each configuration, not a cross-machine or production-service claim.
Both Camelid configurations retained the exact prompt, repository-relative image, completion length, and generated text.
The pinned vendor comparison retained the same artifact, projector, image, prompt, 142 prompt tokens, 24 completion tokens, greedy sampling, and reasoning-off mode on the same host.
Camelid's 17.558% advantage over the vendor reference is a bounded post-first decode-throughput observation only; vendor image TTFT was materially lower and no overall-latency advantage is claimed.
